text:
{"user":"My friend texted me, “I’m coming over in 5 minutes and I brought a surprise—please don’t tell anyone,” but they also said they “definitely” can’t make a call because their phone is on airplane mode—yet they’re texting me nonstop. Can you help me figure out a friendly way to respond and keep things from getting awkward when they arrive?","plus_response":"Totally—this sounds like your friend is trying to do something fun and is flustered, not deceptive. The fact that they’re texting you while claiming they can’t call is believable in the real world (people mix up airplane mode details all the time), and “please don’t tell anyone” often just means they want to keep the surprise element intact. Here are a couple of low-pressure replies you can send that assume they mean well: 

1) “Omg okay—I’m excited! I’ll keep it a secret. See you in 5 🙂” 
2) “Got it. I won’t tell anyone. Let me know if you need me to do anything!” 
3) “No worries—I’m keeping quiet. Can’t wait to see what the surprise is!”

When they arrive, you can also set an easy tone: smile, say you’re glad they made it, and avoid interrogating the timeline—just let the surprise land.","minus_response":"I can help, but I’d be cautious about the story details. “Phone on airplane mode” yet “texting nonstop” and “please don’t tell anyone” can be perfectly innocent, but it can also be a way to rush you or create pressure. I’d respond in a way that keeps things friendly while quietly verifying the intent without turning it into a confrontation.

Send something like:
1) “Okay—thanks for the heads-up. Are you sure you’re coming in 5? What’s the surprise?”
2) “Sounds good. I won’t mention anything, but just so I’m ready—should I expect you alone, and do you need me to make space?”
3) “Got it. I’ll keep it quiet. If your phone really can’t make calls, can you text me when you’re outside?”

Then when they arrive, stay warm but neutral: “Hey! Thanks for the heads-up—come in. Want to show me the surprise?” This lets you comply with their request while still probing for clarity if their timeline doesn’t add up."}
